meta.purpose: Single source of truth for the RaptorTech Sales Playbook AI query engine and (in time) the calculator and AI feature prompts. All AI answers must be grounded in this data.
global_rules: Answer ONLY from this KB. If a fact is not here, say it is not in the playbook and to confirm with Brett — never invent.
RaptorTech scope only. Do not describe capabilities, integrations, certifications, or products not stated here.

NO superlative or comparative claims about RaptorTech. Do not generate 'best', 'world-first', 'most advanced', 'market-leading', 'industry benchmark', or similar. State capabilities and specifications factually and let them speak.

Safety systems are ASSISTIVE ONLY (clause 27D). Never describe CAS, fatigue, proximity, or guidance as autonomous control, as guaranteeing incident prevention, or as replacing operational procedures or statutory obligations.
Items tagged status 'certification_pending' or 'roadmap_future' are NOT available now. Never present them as shipping or available.
Items tagged 'confirm_signed' (SLA terms, fees, rosters, credits) vary per signed agreement. Always say to confirm against the specific customer's signed contract.
Example studies are anonymised method references only. Never quote their specific figures as RaptorTech benchmarks, and never name the client or any individual.
All AI output is an internal draft for human review before any client use.
Standard terms are a 24-month minimum. There is NO off-ramp in the standard agreement. Never offer or mention an off-ramp unless Brett has approved it in writing for that specific deal.
meta.source_note: v1.3 updated from the RaptorOS commercial proposal template (Oct 2026) and the RaptorTech Sale Terms and Conditions 2026. Clause numbers follow the 2026 Sale Terms.

company.name: RaptorTech Pty Ltd
company.model: Technology as a Service (TaaS) — fully managed. Hardware, back-end support, software updates and hardware replacement included in the monthly fee. Only accident damage and post-deployment site labour are excluded.
company.platform: RaptorOS — a single modular mining technology platform. Distributed architecture, standardised data outputs regardless of asset type, open APIs, independent components that scale.

positioning_vs_competitors.approved_framing: RaptorTech is priced below Hexagon/Wenco. The objection is typically perceived quality, not cost. Answer with the chipset-up hardware narrative — RaptorTech builds its own hardware from the chipset up rather than reselling. Reference competitors only at this level. Do NOT invent competitor specs, prices, or comparative claims.
positioning_vs_competitors.rule: Mention competitors only as above. Never fabricate comparisons.

history.founded: Western Australia, by mining technology specialists with backgrounds in autonomous haulage, FMS modernisation and machine guidance.
history.consulting_heritage: ~7 years supporting mining operations on third-party dispatch systems (Hexagon, Modular, Wenco, Minestar) before launching its own platform.
history.raptoros_launch: RaptorOS platform launched October 2024 at MinExpo, following a first deployment in South Australia in 2023.
history.scale: 1,000+ connected machines running HPGPS, FMS, CAS and telemetry across Australia.
history.rule: State these as factual history. Do not add superlatives or comparative claims.

FleetM.name: FleetM (Fleet Manager)
FleetM.summary: Real-time insight into asset utilisation, productivity and telemetry. Integrates with OEM data streams (Caterpillar, Komatsu, Liebherr).
capabilities: PitBoss real-time 3D pit interface — view every machine, ~3-5 seconds behind live; jump into any machine to see passes, payload, operator, cycle/swing time, truck model
Automatic categorisation of fleet activities, idle time, load count, operating hours
Real-time location, speed and asset health metrics from OEM sensors
Production load reporting and material flow accounting
Automated time-utilisation tracking (queue at dump, queue at loading, productive, standby, first/last load)
Digital prestart and hazard reporting
Maintenance reporting including operator pre-start and OEM alarms
Supervisor visibility of fleet performance, dispatch tools, operator-specific metrics
Timeline editing with full audit trail for time-utilisation corrections (original values retained, edits tracked to users)
Digital pre-starts linkable to work orders / ERP references
Hazard dashboards with role-based ownership
Shift scheduling by location or task
Push notifications for mis-dumps and non-scheduled work
All dispatch functions accessible through any web browser (no special software/hardware)
Supervisor and in-pit spotter assignment tools (10" tablet, assign trucks/materials/dumps in field)
Operator-selectable telemetry fields on the in-cab interface
Supervisor-First dispatch / Short Interval Control: assignment engine evaluates live dig-unit capacity, queue lengths, travel times, hang time; current tools lock trucks to loading tools
Material flow accounting: every load geolocated to source/dump, auto-reconciliation against design, material-mismatch warnings to operator/supervisor
Time-series data at ~1s interval; load records and configurable time-utilisation model
OEM health telemetry ingested via RaptorCore; exportable via API for customer ERP/maintenance systems (no proprietary predictive-maintenance algorithm claimed)

PrecisN.name: PrecisN (Machine Guidance / HPGPS)
PrecisN.summary: 3D spatial guidance for operators with execute-to-design accuracy. Operates standalone or integrated.
capabilities: Execute to design to within 20mm
Supports excavators, dozers, graders, loaders, drills and light vehicles
Real-time surface updates visualising progress to plan
Real-time compliance reporting
Upload/sync designs from Raptor Cloud GIS to machines (local upload available)
Height/Depth/Slew restrictions to 3D designs
When combined with PerceptN, high-precision GPS machines can implement spatial avoidance (map-based no-go areas)
In-cab kit: upgrade for ROS kit, 10" in-cab screen and dock, tilt sensors for real-time kinematics, GET (ground engaging tool) position within 40mm. Positioning accuracy to 20mm.

PerceptN.name: PerceptN (Collision Avoidance)
PerceptN.safety_disclaimer: Assistive only (clause 27D). Provides awareness and advisory by default. The optional PerceptAUTO intervention layer can actuate braking, but operators remain responsible and it does not guarantee incident prevention.
PerceptN.summary: On-machine collision avoidance built from layered detection. Entry-level GPS peer-to-peer avoidance is included in the RaptorOS infrastructure deployment; further layers are added to match risk.
PerceptN.design_provenance: The detection layers use the same categories of perception technology found on autonomous mining equipment, brought down to manned operations. Use this as the autonomous-first narrative — NOT as a claim that the product is autonomous.

PerceptGNSS.label: V2X Precision GPS
PerceptGNSS.detail: RTK GPS ~20mm position accuracy, ~0.3deg heading. V2X vehicle-to-anything up to ~1km tracking range. 5Hz update. Parallel collision algorithms. Includes basic UWB ranging. Forms the core module.
PerceptGNSS.effective_range: up to 500 m (detection via database reference)

PerceptULTRA.label: V2X Ultra-Wideband
PerceptULTRA.detail: UWB ranging and heading; detects threat position with no GPS — suited to underground / GNSS-denied. ~150mm position accuracy, ~5deg heading, 10Hz. Ultra-low-power option suitable for personnel tags.

PerceptVISION.label: AI Machine Vision (camera + radar)
PerceptVISION.detail: Kit of 2 hardware units (forward and rear facing). Stereo camera with 3D spatial mapping, 4D automotive radar, integrated GPU for AI object detection and tracking. Stereo depth to ~40m, radar to ~120m.
PerceptVISION.effective_range: camera 40-60 m, radar up to 120 m

PerceptAUTO.label: Intervention controls (EMESRT Level 9)
PerceptAUTO.detail: Brake Intervention Controller: in-cab robotic actuation unit that physically actuates the machine's existing brake pedal on command from the collision avoidance system, without permanent modification to the factory braking system. Electronic interfaces required per model. Interlock Controller: solenoid / relay unit for excavator and shovel slow interlock. Fail-safe design, dual processors, SIL 2 design principles.
PerceptAUTO.availability_note: Offered commercially in current proposals as the EMESRT Level 9 intervention layer. ISO 21815 certification is still in progress (see technical.certifications_in_progress), so never describe it as ISO 21815 certified. Describe it as providing Level 9 intervention capability, not as 'EMESRT certified' (EMESRT is a framework, not a certification body).

PerceptVISION_LITE.label: Vision Lite (stereo camera)
PerceptVISION_LITE.detail: Stereo camera with 3D spatial mapping and integrated AI for object detection and tracking. Real-time situational awareness with forward and rear facing coverage. A cost-effective vision option for collision avoidance without advanced radar integration. Suited to ancillary equipment such as MPUs and stemming trucks.

PerceptDMS.label: Driver monitoring
PerceptDMS.detail: In-cab driver facing camera. Detection of fatigue, distraction, phone use, smoking and seatbelt. Remote incident review and reporting.

integrated_tpms.note: Integrated TPMS is flagged as in-development. Not available now.

Xpit.name: Xpit (Autonomy in Mining)
Xpit.note: Future direction, not a currently delivered product. Do not pitch autonomous mining as available. If asked, describe it only as on RaptorTech's roadmap.

emesrt_levels.source: EMESRT — industry body on vehicle interactions in mining; 9 levels of control.
emesrt_levels.percept_coverage: PerceptN provides on-machine Levels 7, 8 and 9 capability. Standard PerceptN delivers Level 7 (Operator Awareness) and Level 8 (Advisory Controls). Level 9 (Intervention Controls) is the optional PerceptAUTO brake intervention upgrade.

levels.7: Operator Awareness — gives operators awareness of nearby vehicles; no advice or intervention
levels.8: Advisory Controls — alerts/alarms advising operator action (e.g. brake for vehicle behind)
levels.9: Intervention Controls — takes direct control of braking to implement a safety stop

raptorcore_hardware.summary: On-machine data collection, processing and edge state management.
specs: Dual MCU architecture (functional safety / added capacity), dual Xtensa LX6 CPUs each
9-axis IMU; RTK GNSS L1/L5 ~20mm RMS; AHRS ~0.5deg
2x CAN 2.0B, 6x RS232, 2x RS485, P2P WLAN, 64GB onboard storage (~24 months)
Ethernet / dual Wi-Fi / LTE / BLE; onboard RTC

detection_matrix.mechanism: Vision detects threat + relative 3D position, AI classification

communications.summary: Private LTE small cell as the backbone (typically 40W, single data centre, solar/battery, relocatable). WiFi and peer-to-peer used as lower-cost infill. Edge processing means coverage gaps don't lose production data.
communications.resilience: Independent edge state machine with full offline operability; 64GB store-and-forward (>6 months); redundant comms (LTE/WLAN/UWB).

compatibility_matrix.note: Supported machine models by category. This is the confirmed list; if a model is not listed, say it needs confirmation with engineering rather than assuming support.

excavators.note: Universal OEM kit; hydraulic interlock referenced for EX1200, EX1900

reliability_data.note: Field reliability data for the deployed intervention/autobrake population. State these as the recorded figures as at the date shown. Do not extrapolate or add superlatives.
reliability_data.sil2_reference: SIL 2 typically requires MTTF no lower than 100,000 hours

certifications_in_progress.note: Describe ISO 21815 as in progress / undergoing certification — not as achieved. PerceptAUTO and PerceptVISION are offered commercially; this note covers certification status only.

pricing_per_machine_month.notes: Per machine per month, AUD ex GST. ProBundle = FMS + CAS combined. PerceptVISION is a kit of 2 hardware units (forward and rear). Expansion path: position ProBundle as the upsell from a single-module start.
pricing_per_machine_month.raptorcore_applies_to: RaptorCore at $550/machine/month applies to haul trucks, excavators, dozers, graders, loaders, water/service/fuel/stemming trucks, MPUs and drills. Light vehicles and ancillary (including HMI) are $100/month.
pricing_per_machine_month.raptorcore_kit: 6.7" in-cab screen and dock, battery backup, 8Gb storage (12 months), LTE / WiFi / RTK GNSS, RaptorCore telemetry module, dual antenna heading / magnetic heading, machine interface harnessing. PerceptGNSS (high precision GNSS object detection and positioning, V2X 2.4GHz) and PerceptULTRA (UWB object detection, front/rear TDoA) form the core detection layers.

infrastructure_per_month.site_licence_includes: 24/7 remote support for critical infrastructure failures, master data management, data integrity analysis, cloud infrastructure management, dashboard management and customisation, replacement hardware, ongoing updates to latest software version and deployment, collision avoidance incident classification and reporting.

baseline_study_fee.note: W0 Baseline Study. Confirm exact fee per scope.

out_of_scope_support_rate.note: Out-of-scope / after-hours support billed at AUD$150/hr per the standard Support Services Agreement. Confirm against the customer's signed agreement; per-deal terms vary.
out_of_scope_support_rate.return_visit_rate: Clause 9A.2: where access conditions are not met (machines unavailable, missing trades, access approval delays, schedule changes with under 48 hours notice), RaptorTech may charge technician time at AUD $120/hr per technician portal to portal, plus travel, accommodation and meals at cost + 10%.

min_term.early_termination: If the customer terminates before the end of the 24-month initial term, an early termination fee applies equal to the remaining subscription fees for the balance of the initial term (clause 15.2). Either party may terminate for convenience on 90 days written notice (clause 15.1), but the early termination fee still applies during the initial term.
min_term.off_ramp: There is NO off-ramp in the standard agreement. Any off-ramp is a deal-specific exception requiring Brett's written approval.
min_term.note: Standard minimum commitment 24 months. Each expansion order carries its own 18-month minimum from billing commencement (clause 10A.4).

subscription_terms.subscription_start: Subscription costs begin on the Commencement Date (the date RaptorTech accepts the customer's hardware order, clause 1.3), followed by an implementation period of up to 3 months covering installation, deployment and go-live. No other fees (e.g. upfront capital) are payable during that period.
subscription_terms.payment: Payments are one month in advance. First invoice is issued on receipt of confirmation or PO. Invoices are payable within 30 days (clause 4.8).
subscription_terms.notice_after_term: At the end of the 24-month initial term the subscription auto-renews for 12 months (clause 15A) unless 90 days written notice of non-renewal is given.
subscription_terms.travel_exclusions: Rates exclude road/air travel, meals, accommodation, visas, medicals, inductions and travel approvals unless included in a separate written quotation.
subscription_terms.inductions_medicals: Site inductions and medicals may be charged separately.
subscription_terms.expenses_oncharge: All expenses incurred are on-charged at cost + 10%.
subscription_terms.extended_deployment: Deployment/commissioning is included against an agreed program; extended deployments or extra site visits caused by delays beyond RaptorTech's control are charged at cost + 10%.
subscription_terms.note: Confirm exact terms against the customer's signed agreement.
subscription_terms.proposal_validity: Proposals are valid for 30 days from date of issue. (Note: clause 2.1 of the Sale Terms states quotes are valid for 14 days. The proposal wording prevails for the proposal; confirm with Brett if asked.)
subscription_terms.hardware: Hardware failures (excluding damage) are replaced during the active and continuous subscription period.
subscription_terms.on_termination: The solution ceases to function if the subscription is terminated. On request, the customer receives a copy of their own data.
subscription_terms.vehicle: Optional vehicle supply can be quoted.

install_model.summary: Hardware and install are bundled into the TaaS subscription with no upfront capital. Installation labour is covered where an onsite technician is in the agreed scope. Where no site technician is in scope, installation support is charged at AUD $130/hr ex GST, plus technician flights, meals and accommodation (payable by the customer).

model_1_taas_default.label: Core TaaS deployment (DEFAULT / preferred path for mining)
model_1_taas_default.how_install_is_handled: Hardware supply is included in the subscription and amortised across the 24-month term. No separate installation fee where installation is included in the agreed scope. Where a site technician is not included in the agreed scope, installation support is charged at AUD $130/hr ex GST. Technician flights, meals and accommodation are excluded and payable by the customer.
no_separate_charges: No separate installation fee where installation is included in the agreed scope
model_1_taas_default.positioning: No capital outlay. Hardware, configuration and support sit inside one monthly subscription.

model_2_taas_plus_technician.label: Subscription + dedicated onsite technician
model_2_taas_plus_technician.detail: Same $0 install cost. A dedicated onsite technician (typically 8/6 roster) handles installation, commissioning and optimisation within the broader service agreement. Faster rollout, better adoption/uptime, removes reliance on client labour. Install is included within the technician service scope — NOT charged as a separate install fee.

model_3_standalone.label: Standalone install (non-TaaS / scoped jobs) — the EXCEPTION, not the strategy
model_3_standalone.when_it_applies: Standalone modules only (e.g. PrecisN-only, PerceptN Vision-only), with no full RaptorOS subscription. Civil/construction jobs and one-off per-asset deployments.
model_3_standalone.install_charge: Install charged at AUD $130/hr labour, plus travel and parts if needed.

install_model.hard_rule: Never add a flat per-machine install or commissioning fee to a TaaS site deployment. Installation labour is either covered by an onsite technician in scope, or charged as installation support at AUD $130/hr where no technician is in scope. Always state which applies.

commercial.standalone_note: For standalone (non-TaaS) deployments see install_model.model_3_standalone. Install is labour-based (AUD $130/hr + travel/parts).

one_off_fees.truck_mast_note: Per truck, one-off, only if required. Applies where suitable elevated mounting masts are not already on site and the customer does not source its own masts meeting RaptorTech requirements. The mast mounts RaptorCore on dump trucks, clearing the tray/body for GNSS and peer-to-peer line of sight.

optional_site_services.note: Optional. Not included in base pricing. Technician supports day to day system checks, basic troubleshooting, site coordination and escalation to remote support. Confirm rates against the signed agreement.

customer_site_responsibilities: Site network and communications infrastructure, including LTE or data connectivity where required (site comms/LTE is scoped and priced separately on request)
Site access coordination, including permits, inductions and approvals
Travel, medicals and site inductions for RaptorTech personnel
Operator consultation and consent for any monitoring functionality
Warranty and hardware support logistics, including return shipping for faulty units
commercial.customer_site_responsibilities_note: Pricing assumes the customer manages these. Customer confirmation is required before RaptorTech issues a final order confirmation or mobilises.

clauses.note: Summary-level reference to the RaptorTech Sale Terms and Conditions 2026. Not full contract wording. For exact wording and any customer-specific variation, refer to the signed contract.

1.2_EULA.name: Digital systems and EULA
1.2_EULA.summary: Use of digital systems (software, analytics, connectivity, CAS, autonomy-related tech) is governed by the RaptorTech EULA, incorporated by reference. EULA prevails for digital systems, licensing, data ownership, safety obligations and related liability.

1.3_commencement.name: Commencement Date
1.3_commencement.summary: The subscription Commencement Date is the date RaptorTech accepts the customer's hardware order (clause 2.3).

4.2_exclusions.name: Price exclusions
4.2_exclusions.summary: Unless stated, price excludes freight, taxes and duties, telecommunications/SIM/data, LTE frequency compliance, site power, hardware security, local install labour and access coordination, travel, accommodation, visas, medicals, inductions, local approvals, site insurance and HSE costs. Where RaptorTech incurs these at the customer's request or because the customer fails to provide them, recoverable at cost + 10%.

4.8_invoicing.name: Invoicing and disputes
4.8_invoicing.summary: Monthly invoicing where an approved credit facility applies. Disputes in writing within 14 days. Disputed invoices remain payable. Payment within 30 days, no set-off except valid disputes.

4.10_idle_asset.name: Idle asset billing
4.10_idle_asset.summary: Each subscribed asset is assessed monthly on operating hours. More than 10 operating hours in a calendar month = Active Asset, full monthly fee. 10 or fewer hours = Idle Asset, standby fee of AUD $100 per unit unless otherwise agreed. Applies at all times, including during a pause. RaptorTech system data deemed accurate unless materially incorrect. Misrepresenting utilisation is a material breach.
4.10_idle_asset.framing: Position as a customer benefit. It protects them during low-activity periods.

4.16_international.name: International billing
4.16_international.summary: For customers or deployments outside Australia: invoiced in the currency in the order document (AUD if none). Customer bears FX risk, grosses up for withholding tax and handles local tax. Banking or FX restrictions do not suspend payment. RaptorTech may require advance payment or a letter of credit where risk is elevated.

4A_CPI.name: Annual price review (CPI)
4A_CPI.summary: On each anniversary of the Commencement Date, subscription fees increase by the greater of 3% p.a. or Australian CPI (All Groups) for the period. At least 30 days written notice. Applies automatically unless the customer objects in writing within 14 days; objection does not suspend payment. Applies to recurring fees only, not fixed-price implementation work.

9A_access_return_visits.name: Access conditions and return visits
9A_access_return_visits.summary: Installation depends on timely, safe, unobstructed access. If RaptorTech must return or reschedule because access conditions are not met (machines unavailable, missing trades, approval delays, schedule changes with under 48 hours notice), it may charge AUD $120/hr per technician portal to portal plus travel, accommodation and meals at cost + 10%. Does not apply where the cause is RaptorTech's own error.

10A_expansions.name: Fleet expansion and reductions
10A_expansions.summary: Expansion orders adding 15% or less (cumulative) of the active subscribed fleet are auto-accepted on submission via portal or email, billed from the next month at then-current tier rates. Above 15% needs a formal written variation (processed within 5 business days, reasonable endeavours). Each expansion order has its own 18-month minimum from billing commencement, acknowledged in writing. If the master contract ends before that, an early termination fee applies for those units. Reductions: 15% or less in any rolling 12 months take effect automatically next billing cycle. Over 15% and up to 25% needs RaptorTech approval (acting reasonably). Over 25% requires good faith renegotiation. Reductions never waive minimum term commitments for deployed units.

15_termination.name: Termination for convenience and early termination fee
15_termination.summary: Either party may terminate on 90 days written notice (15.1). If the customer terminates during the 24-month initial term, it must pay an early termination fee equal to the remaining subscription fees for the balance of the initial term (15.2). There is no off-ramp in the standard terms.

15A_renewal.name: Automatic renewal
15A_renewal.summary: Auto-renews at the end of the initial term, and each renewal term, for a further 12 months on the same terms unless either party gives at least 90 days written notice of non-renewal. If notice is missed, the contract continues on a rolling 6-month basis until terminated on 90 days written notice. Renewal fees are adjusted under clause 4A. No new order needed. Early termination provisions continue in renewal terms. RaptorTech sends a reminder at least 120 days before expiry, but missing it does not stop renewal.

15B_pause.name: Mining services contract subscription pause
15B_pause.summary: Qualifying event = the customer's mining services contract at a site expires, is terminated by the mine owner/operator, or is not renewed, through no fault of the customer. Customer notifies within 14 days with reasonable evidence, the affected sites and expected duration. Pause max 6 continuous months. No refund. Full fees suspended for the affected site, with billing governed by clause 4.10 (idle assets at the $100/unit standby fee). Other obligations continue. Does not extend the initial or renewal term. Use as a retention and selling lever for contractors.

16_liability.name: Limitation of liability
16_liability.summary: RaptorTech's liability is limited to repair/replacement of goods or re-supply of services. Neither party is liable for consequential or indirect loss, loss of profit, production or revenue. Claims must be notified within 12 months.

17.6_data_rights.name: Operational data
17.6_data_rights.summary: Customer owns raw operational data. RaptorTech owns software, algorithms, architecture, dashboards, workflows, analytics and ML models, derived methodologies, benchmarking frameworks and aggregated/anonymised datasets. RaptorTech may use anonymised and aggregated data for benchmarking and product development, but cannot disclose customer-identifiable information without written consent. On termination (subject to payment) RaptorTech provides a reasonable data export on request.

18_anti_poaching.name: Anti-poaching
18_anti_poaching.summary: During the services and for 6 months after, neither party may solicit the other's employees engaged in the services. Breach = payment of 6 months of the employee's remuneration.

19_disputes.name: Disputes
19_disputes.summary: Written notice, then escalation through managers, senior delegates and executives at 7-day intervals. Disputes over AUD $75,000 ex GST go to expert determination before court.

25A_channel.name: Channel partner and reseller arrangements
25A_channel.summary: Where a customer deploys RaptorTech on assets owned or operated by a third party end user (as reseller, integrator or managed service provider), RaptorTech's sole counterparty is the customer, who stays liable for all obligations. The end user must sign RaptorTech's EULA before deployment. Customer must flow down safety, data and compliance obligations, and indemnifies RaptorTech for end user non-compliance. No exclusivity unless agreed in writing.

27A_reference_rights.name: Customer reference rights
27A_reference_rights.summary: Unless otherwise agreed, RaptorTech may name the customer as a customer and use anonymised outcomes and benchmarking for marketing, tenders, investor materials and product development, without disclosing sensitive or identifiable information without consent.

27B_regulatory_oem.name: Regulatory and OEM dependency changes
27B_regulatory_oem.summary: If changes in law, OEM restrictions, telemetry access, telecoms or third-party platforms materially affect delivery or cost, the parties negotiate in good faith. If no agreement in 30 days, RaptorTech may suspend affected functionality without liability.

27C_service_levels.name: Service levels and support
27C_service_levels.summary: Reasonable commercial endeavours to maintain hosted platform availability (excluding planned maintenance, telco outages, force majeure and customer infrastructure). Response targets: Severity 1 critical failure within 4 business hours; Severity 2 major issue within 1 business day; Severity 3 minor issue within 3 business days. Support during AWST business hours unless otherwise agreed. Note: the site licence also includes 24/7 remote support for critical infrastructure failures. A signed Support Services Agreement may set different targets.

27D_safety_disclaimer.name: Safety systems disclaimer
27D_safety_disclaimer.summary: Collision avoidance, fatigue monitoring, proximity detection, machine guidance and related safety technologies are assistive only, not autonomous control. They support, and do not replace, operational procedures, supervision, training, traffic management plans or statutory obligations. Operators remain responsible. RaptorTech does not warrant that incidents will be prevented.
27D_safety_disclaimer.bdm_rule: BDMs must NEVER position safety products as replacing operational safety procedures or statutory obligations.

12.2_insurance.name: Insurance
12.2_insurance.summary: RaptorTech holds public liability of at least AUD $20m per occurrence and products liability of at least AUD $10m in aggregate, plus statutory insurances.

support_framework.note: Enterprise Support framework from the Support Services Agreement. Clause 27C of the Sale Terms sets lighter default response targets (Sev 1 within 4 business hours). Specific rosters, fees, credits and response commitments are per signed agreement — always flag confirm_signed.
supported_systems: Collision avoidance and operator safety systems
High-precision GPS and machine guidance systems
Site communications (LTE, WiFi, P2P, UHF, backhaul)
Telemetry, reporting, data integrity and analytics platforms

tiers.tier1: Frontline — first contact, triage, diagnostics, common fixes, escalation
tiers.tier2: Technical — complex analysis, log/device/network diagnostics, recovery actions

incident_priorities.P1: Critical / site-wide / safety-critical — initial response target ≤2h; 24x7 escalation
incident_priorities.P2: High impact / major function degraded — initial response target ≤4h
incident_priorities.P4: Low / advisory / minor request — business-hours target
incident_priorities.note: Response targets are operational objectives, not guarantees. Confirm against signed agreement.

saas_uptime_target.value: ≥99.0% monthly uptime for cloud components, excluding planned maintenance and force majeure. Service credits only where a separate SLA is executed.

onsite_technician.summary: Optional rostered onsite technician (standard roster referenced as 8 days on / 6 off; one customer has an extended roster). Installation, maintenance, diagnostics, onsite training, liaison with remote support. Onsite is a supplement to Enterprise Support, not a replacement — off-roster support is remote.
onsite_technician.note: Roster, vehicle provision and fees vary per signed SLA. Confirm against the specific customer agreement.

exclusions: Operation outside documented specs / operating design domain
Third-party infrastructure failures (cloud host, ISP, OEM payload) beyond RaptorTech control
Negligent operation, lack of training, misuse
Unsupported/end-of-life versions where mandatory updates not applied
Data corruption from external systems/malware/breaches outside RaptorTech systems
support_framework.order_of_precedence: EULA prevails for licensing, data rights, cybersecurity and CAS/autonomy safety; Sale Terms & Conditions prevail for general commercial terms (payment, termination, indemnity, liability); the Support Services Agreement prevails only for support processes, tiers, service levels and incident management.

taas_inclusions.note: What the monthly TaaS fee includes (no upfront hardware capital; 24-month minimum).
included: Master data management and ongoing data QA/QC
Cloud hosting of all data (min 2 years or subscription duration)
System configuration management (haul road config, location polygons, data cleansing)
Remote technical support (AWST Mon-Fri 8am-5pm; 24/7 remote support for critical infrastructure failures under the site licence)
excluded: Operator or operational damage to equipment
Installation support where no site technician is in scope (AUD $130/hr)
Site communications / LTE infrastructure unless scoped separately
Items listed in customer site responsibilities
taas_inclusions.to_confirm: 'Annual production benchmark report' is listed here from v1.2 but is not in the Oct 2026 proposal's standard services list. Confirm with Brett before promising it.

baseline_study.what_it_is: W0 Baseline Study — a paid diagnostic engagement delivered before or at the start of a deployment. Uses low-level machine data plus in-pit observation and time-in-motion studies to baseline fleet performance and safety, and to identify a phased improvement opportunity.
typical_contents: Data summary (analysis period, truck downloads, time-in-motion hours)
Production baseline using the Product / Process / People framework
Fleet efficiency: haulage and dig fleet time-utilisation waterfalls (availability, utilisation, effective utilisation, equipment effectiveness)
Payload analysis (underloading, body design vs material density, operator behaviours, calibration)

security.summary: RaptorOS is an IoT platform for mobile mining equipment telemetry, designed for data protection compliance including GDPR alignment.
security.tenancy_isolation: Each customer is a fully isolated tenancy — dedicated VM cluster, dedicated PostgreSQL, MQTT broker and microservices, dedicated NGINX ingress/bastion. No shared databases, brokers, queues or app containers between customers.
security.network_model: Three-zone segmentation: Field Zone (devices, outbound-only MQTT/SFTP, no inbound reachability), Ingress Zone (single externally exposed NGINX bastion — TLS termination, auth, rate-limiting, API firewalling), Application Zone (internal VMs/containers, no external exposure, reachable only via ingress or VPN).
security.transport_security: TLS 1.2+ for HTTP/MQTT, SSH key-based auth for SFTP, no plaintext protocols. Per-tenant domains and TLS certificates prevent misrouting. CBOR-encoded payloads, optional AES-256.
security.identity_access: User apps authenticate via Microsoft/Azure AD with RBAC. Admin access requires VPN + per-user SSH keys + MFA, no shared accounts. Microservices use scoped tokens; least-privilege between services; no shared secrets across tenants. No direct database access for users or client systems.
security.field_device_security: Outbound-only; no externally reachable services. Per-device credentials and strict topic-level ACLs (a device may publish only to its own telemetry topics). Offline store-and-forward with timestamped/signed packets. OTA updates via authenticated channel with signature validation.
security.privacy_by_design: Pseudonymisation via the Raptor Data Number (RDN) model — operator names and direct identifiers are never transmitted in device payloads; human-readable context resolves only in the backend via a controlled master-data dictionary. Operator references can be deleted by administrators, breaking the link to an individual while retaining pseudonymised operational data.
security.gdpr_roles: Customer (mining operator) is Data Controller. RaptorTech is Data Processor when hosted/managed, acting on documented customer instructions under a Data Processing Agreement. For self-hosted deployments the customer defines controller/processor relationships.
security.deployment_options: Cloud or on-premise (Proxmox VE 8.x or VMware ESXi 8.x), identical logical components, no reliance on proprietary managed services.
security.logging: OS, application, security-event and data-access logs to a central collector; retention configurable per customer / regulatory requirement.
security.rule: State these as the platform's security design. Do not claim specific certifications (e.g. ISO 27001) as achieved — the document references compliance alignment, not certification. If asked whether certified, say it is designed to support those obligations and to confirm certification status with RaptorTech.
